key_insight: A mean-flow adjoint framework with homogenized lattice Boltzmann and Brinkman penalization enables practical sensitivity analysis for porous-cylinder flows from steady to turbulent regimes without relying on full transient checkpointing.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more tractable way to compute design gradients for drag and energy-dissipation optimization in complex fluid systems, especially when unsteady or turbulent dynamics make standard adjoints expensive or unstable.
method: Use HLBM to represent porous cylinders as locally homogenized porous media via Brinkman penalization.
Formulate a mean-flow adjoint to reduce memory burden and avoid gradient divergence in unsteady/chaotic flows.
Employ automatic differentiation to generate adjoint kernels with SGS LES terms and compare against frozen turbulence assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic study spanning steady laminar, unsteady, and turbulent flow cases, including a proof-of-concept at Re = 3900.
watch_item: Mean-flow and frozen-turbulence approximations may limit gradient fidelity in strongly nonstationary turbulence, so validation against direct sensitivities or experiments is important.
paper_title: Mean-Flow Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis of Unsteady Flow Around Porous Cylinders Using a Homogenized Lattice Boltzmann Method
